name: a despicable person
overview: A despicable person is a male figure identified as the leader of the kingdom of the north, as described in Daniel 11:21. Although his tribe is not specified, he is widely understood to be Antiochus Epiphanes. His role as a ruler in this prophetic context marks him as a significant adversary in biblical prophecy.
namesAndTitles: The single name attributed to this figure is 'a despicable person,' which is a descriptive title rather than a personal name. This designation emphasizes his negative character and role as portrayed in Daniel 11:21 without indicating a given name from God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for this person beyond his role as leader of the kingdom of the north. No additional relationships are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: This figure is significant in biblical prophecy as a symbol of opposition against God's people, representing a ruler who embodies despicable qualities. Identified likely as Antiochus Epiphanes, he fulfills the role of a hostile leader whose actions are pivotal in the unfolding of end-time events described in Daniel. His portrayal serves as a warning and a part of God's sovereign plan revealed through prophecy.
